deductible: A deductible is the amount you pay for care before your plan starts to pay.
copay: A copay is a fixed amount you pay for a visit or service.
coinsurance: Coinsurance is the share of the cost you pay after the deductible, often a percentage.
allowed amount: The allowed amount is the most your plan counts for a service. In-network providers agree to it.
EOB: An EOB (explanation of benefits) is a statement from your insurance. It shows what was billed, what the plan allowed and paid, and what you owe. It is not a bill.
in-network: In-network means the provider has an agreement with your plan about prices.
out-of-network: Out-of-network means the provider has no price agreement with your plan.
prior authorization: Prior authorization is approval from your plan before certain care.
balance billing: Balance billing is when a provider bills you for the difference between its price and the allowed amount.
billed amount: The billed amount is the price the provider lists before insurance.
patient responsibility: Patient responsibility is the part of the cost that you owe.
claim: A claim is a request for payment that the provider sends to your insurance.
denial: A denial is when the plan decides not to pay for a service.
appeal: An appeal is a request that the plan reconsider a denial.
itemized bill: An itemized bill lists every charge with its code, date and price.
